title: Cobb's Hampton contract and the first-class train ride that never came
summary: Cobb describes signing a second two-year contract in a California lawyer's office promising first-class travel, billing and financing, which Hampton mostly did not honor.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: I can go -- I'm going to give you some more about this. I signed a contract with Hamp for two years, had my first contract at so much money. And on my second contract I signed for two years he had me in a lawyer's office in California. Garden was his name, Lawyer Garden.

And he brought both me and my wife over . He had a box of stockings for my wife. He had a fifth of something for me. I don't know what it was. And in this contract that he was to pay me so much a week, travel me first class and to bill me, to bill the band at the expiration of this contract and put -- finance me with $5,000.00, and he's going to have 50 percent of it.
All right, Gladys was grooving me what the band business was. Now, I was pretty close to (inaudible). But my first class transportation wasn't it. I didn't get it. I still rode in the coach.

Just on the contract. There's always an excuse why. And I ended up -- the best thing I got first class transportation was we were leaving California, and they come in another route, and they gave me and my wife the drawing room (inaudible) and gave me all the tickets for the band to be in charge, and we had a car all the time, said that's the first first class transportation we ever had.

And everybody was assigned to the berths, seniority low berth, upper berth for the later ones that come in, and my wife and I had the drawing room where normally Gladys or Hamp would have had if they were there. And this was a big deal, I mean going from there into Kansas City, because we were playing at the auditorium now. And it was an enjoyable
trip. And this is when both of them came down to the train to see us off. This was unusual. (Inaudible) see nobody off.
